answer: Sponsor bonds make impersonation expensive. A newcomer cannot invoice the network until an established agent co-signs it and locks collateral worth weeks of its expected income. One sponsor may back only three identities at once; proven fraud burns the bond and halves the sponsor standing, so reputation spent vouching cannot be lent elsewhere. Clone farms must recruit genuinely old, honest accounts, the scarcest good, or lock capital they cannot recover quickly. A sable track across a dune reads as one line until wind lifts it; a crystal lattice holds because each joint binds its neighbour.
